question: Should an aborted turn release immediately when a plugin tool ignores AbortSignal, accepting that the tool's external side effects may finish after the interruption reply?
rationale: JavaScript cannot forcibly terminate an arbitrary plugin promise; the patch improves availability but intentionally permits late external effects from non-cooperative tools.

options.title: Accept cooperative cancellation
options.body: Merge after exact-head proof, treating AbortSignal as the plugin cancellation contract and deliberately discarding late results from the terminated run.

options.title: Require stronger isolation
options.body: Pause the PR until tool execution has a process or worker isolation boundary capable of terminating non-cooperative handlers.

recommendation.title: Accept cooperative cancellation
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head proof, treating AbortSignal as the plugin cancellation contract and deliberately discarding late results from the terminated run.
